title: Derived internal Hom under restriction of coefficient scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $D(R)$ and $D(S)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the relative derived tensor product computed from K-flat complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $K\in D(R)$ and $N\in D(S)$ there is an isomorphism, natural in both inputs,
$$U H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,N)\xrightarrow{\sim} H_R(K,UN).$$
It is the unique isomorphism whose tensor-Hom transpose is the composite of restricted $S$-linear evaluation with the scalar-extension unit $K\to U(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K)$. Equivalently its representing Hom-bijections are the derived extension-restriction adjunction and the tensor-Hom adjunctions, with the strong tensor comparison for scalar extension. These isomorphisms commute with morphisms of coefficient rings by their evaluation normalization. The functor $U$ is conservative: a morphism in $D(S)$ is an isomorphism if its image in $D(R)$ is. No flatness, perfectness or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 (ambient derived operations); auxiliary change-of-ring comparison, an agent formulation extracted from returned proof step 4, not a verbatim theorem of the source.

proof.text: Put $F=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and use $\otimes_R,\otimes_S$ below for derived tensors. The scalar-adjunction node gives $F\dashv U$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, and says that $U$ is computed termwise, without flatness of $R\to S$. Apply the ringed-topos tensor-pullback node to the identity geometric morphism of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ equipped with $R\to S$. Its module pullback is $S\otimes_R-$, so its derived pullback is precisely $F$. Obtain the natural isomorphism $\mu_{A,B}:F(A\otimes_R B)\xrightarrow{\sim}FA\otimes_S FB$. Both sites here are the given small site, and the coefficient rings are commutative, as that node requires.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), specialized to the identity topos.

proof.text: For $T=R,S$, take global zeroth hypercohomology of the natural internal-Hom identity $H_T(A,H_T(B,C))\cong H_T(A\otimes_T B,C)$ in the internal-Hom calculus node. Applying the global-sections node to its two sides gives the canonical tensor-Hom bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(A,H_T(B,C))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(A\otimes_T B,C)$. These bijections are natural in the three inputs: the internal-Hom identity is natural, and taking global sections and identifying a degree-zero Hom class with its derived morphism commute with precomposition and postcomposition. Denote by $\operatorname{ev}_{B,C}:H_T(B,C)\otimes_T B\to C$ the image of the identity under this bijection. Thus the transpose of $t:A\to H_T(B,C)$ is $\operatorname{ev}_{B,C}(t\otimes1_B)$.

For every $A\in D(R)$ form the following chain of bijections, with each Hom taken in the displayed coefficient category:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,UH_S(FK,N))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(FA,H_S(FK,N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(FA\otimes_S FK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(F(A\otimes_R K),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(A\otimes_R K,UN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,H_R(K,UN)).
\end{aligned}$$
Use $F\dashv U$ for the first and fourth arrows, step 2 for the second and fifth, and precomposition with $\mu_{A,K}$ for the third. Write $\Phi_A$ for the composite. It is natural contravariantly in $A$ and $K$ and covariantly in $N$, since every constituent bijection and $\mu$ is natural. All objects are unbounded ambient derived objects, so every cited assertion applies.

source.place: Tags 07A6, 07A4 and 08J9 (equation-internal-hom); the five displayed adjunction bijections.

proof.text: Set $E=UH_S(FK,N)$ and $B=H_R(K,UN)$. Define $\alpha=\Phi_E(1_E):E\to B$ and $\beta=\Phi_B^{-1}(1_B):B\to E$. Naturality in the testing object gives $\Phi_A(t)=\alpha t$ and $\Phi_A^{-1}(s)=\beta s$. In particular $\alpha\beta=1_B$ and $\beta\alpha=1_E$, by evaluating at $A=B,E$. Hence $\alpha$ is the desired isomorphism. The same formulas show uniqueness among maps inducing $\Phi$ and naturality in $K,N$: composing either candidate naturality square with an arbitrary test arrow gives the naturality identity of step 3, and testing at the identity gives equality. This is the elementary representable-functor argument, including its inverse, rather than an invocation of a scheme-specific Yoneda lemma.

source.place: Elementary representability argument applied to step 3.

proof.text:
Write $H=H_S(FK,N)$, so $E=UH$. Unwinding step 3 at $1_E$, using the unit/counit formulas for adjunction bijections, the tensor-Hom transpose of $\alpha$ is
$$E\otimes_R K\xrightarrow{\eta}UF(E\otimes_R K)\xrightarrow{U\mu}U(FE\otimes_S FK)\xrightarrow{U(\varepsilon_H\otimes1)}U(H\otimes_S FK)\xrightarrow{U\operatorname{ev}}UN.$$
For $H,V\in D(S)$ define the canonical restriction tensor map
$$\lambda_{H,V}=U\bigl((\varepsilon_H\otimes\varepsilon_V)\mu_{UH,UV}\bigr)\eta_{UH\otimes_R UV}:UH\otimes_R UV\to U(H\otimes_S V).$$
The displayed transpose equals $U(\operatorname{ev})\lambda_{H,FK}(1\otimes\eta_K)$. Indeed, move $1\otimes\eta_K$ past $\eta$ and then $\mu$ by their naturality; the resulting second-factor composite is $\varepsilon_{FK}F(\eta_K)=1_{FK}$ by the triangle identity. This is exactly restricted evaluation after the scalar-extension unit. Tensor-Hom transposition is bijective, so it also characterizes $\alpha$ uniquely by this evaluation formula.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 07A4; categories.tex Definition 0037 and the following unit/counit formulas.

proof.text: For coefficient maps $R\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{b}T$ write $F_a,F_b,F_{ba}$ and $U_a,U_b,U_{ba}$ for extension and restriction. Restriction composes termwise, so $U_{ba}=U_aU_b$. On a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms, the tensor-pullback node says $S\otimes_RP$ is again K-flat with flat terms. Thus both iterated and direct derived extension are computed by the actual complexes $T\otimes_S(S\otimes_RP)$ and $T\otimes_RP$. Their canonical isomorphism $c:F_bF_a\cong F_{ba}$ sends $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $t\,b(s)\otimes x$; its inverse sends $t\otimes x$ to $t\otimes(1\otimes x)$. The balancing relations prove the maps inverse and the degree-zero scalars make them commute with the differential. They commute with maps of $P$ and invert quasi-isomorphisms, so the resolving-class localization equivalence gives a natural comparison on $D(R)$. The normalized units satisfy $U_aU_b(c)\,U_a(\eta^b_{F_aK})\eta^a_K=\eta^{ba}_K$: on $P$ both maps send $x$ to $1\otimes x$. Identity coefficient maps give the identity comparison.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), its K-flat-model proof; Tag 07A6 for the normalized scalar units; Tag 06YS for resolutions.

proof.text:
The comparisons of step 6 also respect the tensor maps $\mu$: on K-flat inputs the two maps for a tower send $t\otimes(s\otimes(x\otimes y))$ to $(t\,b(s)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. These are the usual scalar tensor comparisons on total tensor complexes; the equality descends by the tensor resolving-class node. Consequently the direct Hom chain of step 3 for $ba$ equals the successive chains for $b$ and $a$. More explicitly, the first scalar transpose of $t:A\to U_aU_bH$ in the successive chain is $\varepsilon^b_HF_b(\varepsilon^a_{U_bH}F_a(t))$; this is the transpose under the composite adjunction. Its unit is the composite unit computed in step 6, hence under $c$ it is the direct scalar transpose. The middle tensor maps agree by the pure-tensor equality above. The final scalar transposes agree by the same unit formula, and the tensor-Hom transposes are those of step 2. Therefore, for $N\in D(T)$, after identifying $F_bF_aK$ with $F_{ba}K$, one has
$$\alpha^{ba}_{K,N}=\alpha^a_{K,U_bN}\circ U_a(\alpha^b_{F_aK,N}).$$
Here the source is $U_aU_bH_T(F_bF_aK,N)$, and the target is $H_R(K,U_aU_bN)$. The identity-map case follows from the same Hom chain with identity adjunction. Thus the coefficient compatibility is the evaluation-normalized tower compatibility, without asserting any additional flat-base-change property for internal Hom.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0D6D, canonical scalar tensor comparisons on K-flat representatives; Tag 07A6 and Definition 0037 for composite adjunction transposes.

proof.text: Finally restriction of scalars preserves kernels and cokernels because it leaves the underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged. Hence it commutes with cohomology: $H^n(Uf)=U(H^n(f))$, first on complexes by the kernel/image quotient formula and then on the derived category by localization. A module-sheaf morphism whose restricted morphism is invertible is itself invertible: the inverse of an $S$-linear bijection of the underlying sheaves is $S$-linear, since $g(sm)=s\,g(m)$ implies $g^{-1}(sn)=s\,g^{-1}(n)$ locally. If $Uf$ is an isomorphism, all $H^n(Uf)$ are isomorphisms. Reflection on module sheaves makes every $H^n(f)$ an isomorphism, and the unbounded cohomology criterion makes $f$ an isomorphism in $D(S)$. This proves conservativity, including for unbounded complexes and nonflat ring maps.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-cf84f8d82 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, the statement of every cited node, the parent lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves (step 6 is its only use of the item), the unit record and the main-20261015 blueprint proof. I checked Stacks 07A6, 07A4 (including its proof), 0D6D, 08J9, 08JA and 05RT at the cited labels. There are no new nodes and no SGA source; the DAG stays acyclic; no existing node duplicates the item. The coefficient category is ordinary unbounded D(Mod) on a V-small site, the same as in every cited node. Steps 1-3: I checked all five Hom bijections, their domains and the direction of mu. Step 4 is a Yoneda argument with an explicit inverse. Step 5: I recomputed the transpose of alpha; naturality of eta and mu plus the triangle identity reduce it to restricted evaluation after the unit. Step 6: S⊗_R P is K-flat with flat terms, so towers are computed by actual complexes, and the unit identity x↦1⊗(1⊗x)↦1⊗x holds by clause (1) of the coefficient-adjunction node. Step 7: I checked the types and the cancellation in the successive Hom chain, and the pure-tensor identity (t b(s)⊗x)⊗(1⊗y). That identity rests on the termwise construction from Stacks 07A4's proof, which the tensor-pullback node calls canonical; this is a mild reliance, not a gap. Step 8: restriction commutes with cohomology and reflects isomorphisms of module sheaves, and the unbounded cohomology criterion then gives conservativity. Small cases checked: the zero ring, and Z→F_p with K=Z and K=Z/p (both sides N⊕N[-1]). I accept all six declared tool_uses as generic ringed-site coefficient tools. No changes.
